corrections.text: The article says Google Cloud's Hydrogen page calls the model "a short-term generally available (GA) release subject to a minimum 45-day retirement notice policy". That wording is not on the Hydrogen page (docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/models/gemini/4-hydrogen, read November 13, 2026), which lists only "Launch stage: GA" and "Release date: November 12, 2026". It paraphrases Google Cloud's model-versions page (cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/model-versions), which lists gemini-4-hydrogen among "Models available for shorter availability periods" and says that when Google Cloud schedules such a model for retirement it posts a fixed date "that gives you at least 45 days to migrate".

The article reports the Google Cloud pricing page's $0.75 and $3.75 for 3.8 Flash through December 31, 2026 and $2.00 and $10.00 for Argon through November 30, 2026 without saying how they are delivered. The page's footnote reads "Promotional pricing provided through 50% credits back on net spend on select models within a given period", so these figures are promotional prices provided through credits, not a lower standard rate.
